values.value: Thinking only about your marketing emails, which would be rebuilt as Content Builder templates and assets: how many email templates are in real use, how much of each is custom modules and HubL doing real logic rather than standard modules and copy, and how many language variants are maintained? Landing pages and site pages are a separate question later on, so leave them out here.

[{"value":1,"label":"A large template and module library that emails are assembled from, with HubL macros, includes and loops doing real logic inside the email, and every template maintained in several language variants."},{"value":2,"label":"A module library editors compose emails from, with HubL conditionals and CRM-association lookups doing real work. Reuse is genuine, so the target-side block library has to exist before content moves."},{"value":3,"label":"Some custom modules and conditional HubL in emails, but the logic is over the contact's own properties and rewrites cleanly into AMPscript and a Data Extension lookup."},{"value":4,"label":"Templates and copy only, few enough to rebuild deliberately, with personalisation that is merge fields and nothing more."}]

Ask for two counts and one ratio: email templates used in the last 12 months, modules ranked by usage IN EMAILS (not across the site), and how many of those templates exist in more than one language. The estimate is per construct and per template, not per email. Do NOT count landing pages, site pages or blog templates here — whether any of that is even moving is the cms_scope_expectation probe, not this slot.
Useful to have to hand: how many email templates you have used in the last 12 months, which custom modules appear in those emails, and how many of the templates exist in more than one language.

reference/ma-migrator-capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — hubl_templating's severity_by_target, quoted because it is the entire reason these anchors differ from hubspot__mcn's: "Major for both, for different reasons. Classic SFMC: AMPscript is comparably expressive, so most HubL constructs have SOME analogue — it is a rewrite, not a redesign. SFMC Next: there is no scripting language at all, so expressive HubL escalates toward blocker." Also custom_modules, "Classic SFMC: content blocks and template slots recover part of the reuse", which is what option 2's library-build clause prices. capabilities/platforms/sfmc.yaml — actions.email_send declares personalization and dynamic_content supported, i.e. the primitives the rewrite lands on exist. THE RECALIBRATION, stated plainly: an estate of custom modules and expressive HubL scores 3 here and 2 on hubspot__mcn. That is not generosity, it is the manifest's own severity split; scoring it 2 on both would have said the two targets cost the same to rebuild against, which is the one thing the manifest explicitly denies. THE RESCOPE, and why HubDB left these anchors: HubL is HubSpot's templating language and custom modules are the blocks built from it, and both are used in two places that migrate differently. Marketing emails are rebuilt in Content Builder by this engagement, so they are readiness and they are scored. Landing pages, site pages, blog and HubDB-driven pages are HubSpot CMS, and in a marketing-automation move to Marketing Cloud Engagement the client typically keeps HubSpot CMS or moves the web estate as a separate programme with a separate sponsor — reference/ma-migrator-capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml, sequences_out_of_scope's severity_by_target states the principle for the analogous case, "the severity comes from the scope and budget boundary, not from a technical asymmetry". Scoring web-estate readiness inside an eight-slot marketing-automation instrument overstated the engagement, and it did it in the direction that hurts: a client who keeps their website on HubSpot was marked down for content nobody was being asked to move. HubDB therefore no longer sits at option 1. It has not been dropped: whether that content is expected to move is now asked directly and unscored as cms_scope_expectation in instrument/migration-accelerator/supplements/hubspot_context.yaml, and the hubdb_dependency callout below is reframed to read as conditional on that answer — which is where a scope boundary belongs, since a 1-4 on someone else's programme is a number with no owner.
